newsitem.title: JAPAN: Landslide in southern Japan kills at least nine.
newsitem.headline: Landslide in southern Japan kills at least nine.

text.p: A landslide triggered by heavy rain killed at least nine people and left about 13 missing on Thursday when a torrent of mud and rocks swept over a village on Japan's southern Kyushu island, police reported.
A police spokesman said the mountain landslide tumbled over Harihara village in Kagoshima Prefecture, 985 km (615 miles) southwest of Tokyo, around 12.50 a.m. (1550 GMT) on Thursday.
"We now have nine people confirmed dead and 13 missing," a Kagoshima Prefectural Police spokesman told Reuters.
The landslide buried 15 homes with a total of 40 residents.
The village, which is home to 80 families, is located on the Harihara River near the city of Izumi.
Japan's Meteorological Agency said the area had received 800 millimetres (32 inches) of rain in the past few days, one-third of the area's normal rainfall for an entire year.
Rain continues to pour down in the area and rescue attempts have been halted because of fears of more landslides, the police spokesman said.
Kagoshima Governor Tatsuro Suga asked for military help in handling the disaster.
The area is designated as landslide-prone and a barrier to prevent landslides was under construction and near completion about 100 meters (yards) away from the buried village.
Another landslide on Wednesday night in neighbouring Kumamoto Prefecture buried nine people under mud but they were all rescued, the police spokesman said.
Last December, 20 people died in another landslide in Kagoshima Prefecture.
